Proposal 6a: For the eight non-Measurement Performance Requirement-related test cases that lack the NOTE in RAN4 spec (highlighted in Orange and Green with black font in Table 1), a CR shall be submitted to RAN4 to introduce the NOTE. For the five test cases highlighted in Orange with black font in Table 1, TS 38.533 shall be revised with RAN4 dependency. Proposal 6b: Following the approach taken for the four green-highlighted test cases, revise TS 38.533 independently of RAN4 to introduce the NOTE for the five orange-highlighted black-font test cases in Table 1. The test cases in red font in the table above are Measurement Performance Requirement test cases. The majority of Measurement Performance Requirement test cases in both RAN4 and RAN5 5G RRM specs already include this NOTE, including test cases in TS 38.533 sections 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.7 and 8.5.2 which shall be dependent on the NR band of the target cell as specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. Observation 8: The majority of Measurement Performance Requirement test cases in both RAN4 and RAN5 5G RRM specs include a NOTE indicating that "The UE is only required to be tested in one of the supported test configurations", including test cases in TS 38.533 sections 4.7, 5.7, 6.7, 7.7 and 8.5.2 which shall be dependent on the NR band of the target cell as specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. However, there are exceptions: Five such test cases lack this NOTE in RAN4 spec; Four such test cases lack this NOTE in RAN5 spec; One such test case lacks this NOTE in RAN4 spec but includes it in RAN5 spec. According to GCF Conformance Assessment Table 3.101.0_20260508_r004 [1], all GCF LTE RRM test cases related to Measurement Performance Requirements are from TS 36.521‑3 section 9 and shall be tested on all supported bands (i.e., all supported FDD bands and all supported TDD bands), which is consistent with TS 36.521‑3 clause 3A.3.4. However, for 5G RRM—as shown in the table below—some Measurement Performance Requirement test cases require testing on all supported bands, while others only require testing on a single band (either one FDD band or one TDD band). Observation 9: According to GCF Conformance Assessment Table 3.101.0_20260508_r004 [1]: For LTE RRM: All Measurement Performance Requirement test cases require testing on all supported bands (i.e., all supported FDD bands and all supported TDD bands), which is consistent with TS 36.521‑3 clause 3A.3.4. For 5G RRM (SA FR1): All Measurement Performance Requirement test cases require testing on all supported bands (FDD + TDD), except for three E-UTRAN measurement test cases that only require testing on one band, which is consistent with TS 38.533 section 3A.6 but inconsistent with the NOTE in the Supported Test Configurations Tables. For 5G RRM (inter-RAT): All Measurement Performance Requirement test cases only require testing on a single band, which is inconsistent with TS 38.533 section 3A.6 but consistent with the NOTE in the Supported Test Configurations Tables. For 5G RRM (NTN): All Measurement Performance Requirement test cases only require testing on a single band, which is not specified in TS 38.533 section 3A.6. ice certification schedule per RP-171154 [1] (WID for UE Conformance Test Aspects – 5G system with NR & LTE), toward our 3x commercial launch. Per RP-171154, the target completion date of New Specs for NSA is TSG #80 (June-18), and target completion date of Impacted Existing TSs is TSG #82 (Dec-18). We understand that delays in inputs from RAN4 (as highlighted by the pending responses for the 3 remaining LSs mentioned in Section 1 and Table-1 in the Annex) will jeopardize this planned schedule. However, AT&T would greatly appreciate it if, upon reception of these inputs from RAN4, RAN5 would expedite the RF test specs in the 521-series identified in RP-171154 by June 2018 and key elements of RRM/Demod test specs by September 2018. In order to achieve this goal, we have identified the following five key elements of RRM/Demod that need to have test cases for verification: Physical RF/RRM/RF Conformance RF OTA Performance 5G Protocols/NAS/Dual Connectivity/Signaling conformance 5G/LTE Network Selection 5G Data Performance AT&T requests RAN5 to expedite the RF test specs in the 521 series identified in RP-171154 by June 2018 and key elements of RRM/Demod (identified in Section 2) by September 2018.

From the offline email discussions, RAN5 identified the following requirements: Machine-readable format (e.g., PICS) Tables in JSON format (test configuration tables) Support for specification attachments in ZIP format (e.g., 38.903) Automation capability (e.g., RRM TT) Maintain only the newest version of the specification (most RAN5 specs) Use of intermediate revisions Ability to combine CRs into “Jumbo” CRs Extractable definitions for cross-spec and external use (e.g., ASN.1) Easy maintenance and cross-referencing of extra-large tables (e.g., 38.523-2) Automated alignment of bands/band configurations between RAN4 and RAN5 (e.g., Excel in PRD21) Most of the identified advantages, disadvantages, and requirements are common across all 3GPP groups. Based on the current review, the RAN5-specific requirements appear to be well covered in the overall discussion. Nevertheless, RAN5 participation will remain important in upcoming calls on Objectives 2 and 3 to ensure RAN5 interests are fully addressed.

{"chunk_id":"R5-232374-002","collection":"ran5_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["CAICT"],"tdocNumber":"R5-232374","title":"Discussion on spurious emission for UE co-existence requirement"},"point_id":"9228635459858966649"}
The inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs also exists for other requirements, e.g., MOP, OoBB, Narrow band blocking and etc, and RAN5 spec does not consider the inconsistencies for other requirements except spurious emission for UE co-existence. Currently most of the new UEs under testing in test labs are still R15 UEs, and only a few of them are R16 UEs. If RAN5 spec considers the inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs, more and more UEs will be blocked to enter certain country or region’s market as they will cause unacceptable interference to co-existing systems, and the n50 and n78 R15 UEs have to meet some unnecessary spurious emission requirements for protected bands that have been recognized as not necessary. It is more serious for LTE as currently new LTE UEs under testing in test labs can be of any release from Rel-8 to Rel-16, and most of them are Rel-15 or backward (e.g., Rel-9, Rel-10, Rel-11, Rel-12. Rel-13, Rel-15). Bands are Release independent in 3GPP, and RAN5 only maintain one Release of spec. Just as what MOP, OoBB, Narrow band blocking and other test cases have done, Spurious emission for UE co-existence test case does not need to include Release information in minimum requirements and test requirements. Proposal 2: RAN5 shall take the latest Release of RAN4 spec as reference for the requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence and remove the Release information in minimum requirements and test requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence. New bands/new CBWs/or new PCs introduced to later Releases can be excluded if there is no interested operator in RAN5. Proposal 3: Minimum requirements and test requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence in TS 38.521-1/-2/-3 and TS 36.521-1 shall be updated as per Proposal 1 and Proposal 2.

ing implementation cost and rollout time. Server-side conformance testing is currently not in scope of 3GPP RAN5. It has resulted in pausing all work for MCPTT, MCVideo, and MCData server test cases which were endorsed by RAN5 and approved by RAN plenaries in Rel-13 and Rel-16 WIDs for mission critical services. It will be beneficial to discuss and agree on a way forward to resume work on MCPTT, MCVideo, and MCData server test cases. Following proposals may be potential way forward: Proposal 1: Accept that some human-controlled devices are able to act as Mission Critical Services servers, exist outside of the core network, and can therefore fit within the current scope of RAN5. or Proposal 2: Extend the scope of RAN5 to include Mission Critical Services server conformance testing which would enable incorporating MCPTT, MCVideo, and MCData server test cases in RAN5 specs.
